# Jubilees Chapter 28 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob's marriages; the birth of the twelve sons

---

**28:1** In the forty-third jubilee, in the second year of the first week, Jacob came to the land of the east, to Laban the brother of his mother Rebekah, and he stayed with him.

**28:2** Laban said to him: "You shall not serve me for nothing. Tell me, what shall your wages be?" Jacob had not yet been with him a full month.

**28:3** Laban had two daughters: the name of the older was Leah and the name of the younger was Rachel. Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form.

**28:4** Jacob loved Rachel and said to Laban: "I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter."

**28:5** Laban said: "It is better that I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me."

**28:6** Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him like only a few days because of his love for her.

**28:7** In the first year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, Jacob said to Laban: "Give me my wife, for my time is fulfilled, that I may go in to her."

**28:8** Laban prepared a feast and took his older daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob as wife. Jacob went in to her, not knowing that she was Leah.

**28:9** In the morning, behold, it was Leah. Jacob said to Laban: "What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?"

**28:10** Laban said: "In our place it is not the practice to give the younger before the older. Complete the bridal week for this one, and I will also give you the other in exchange for another seven years of service."

**28:11** Jacob did so and completed her week. In the second year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as wife.

**28:12** Jacob went in to Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served Laban another seven years.

**28:13** When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

**28:14** Leah conceived and bore a son, and she named him Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month in the first year.

**28:15** In the third year she bore Simeon; in the fourth year she bore Levi; and in the fifth year she bore Judah.

**28:16** When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, she envied her sister and said to Jacob: "Give me children, or I will die."

**28:17** Jacob was angry with Rachel and said: "Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?"

**28:18** She said: "Here is my servant Bilhah; go in to her, that she may bear on my behalf, and through her I too may have children."

**28:19** She gave him her servant Bilhah as wife. He went in to her, and she conceived and bore a son; Rachel named him Dan.

**28:20** Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son, and Rachel named him Naphtali.

**28:21** When Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, she took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as wife. Zilpah bore Jacob a son, and Leah named him Gad.

**28:22** Zilpah bore again, and Leah named him Asher.

**28:23** In the days of the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah: "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."

**28:24** She said: "Is it not enough that you have taken my husband? And now you want to take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said: "Very well; he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."

**28:25** When Jacob came home from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him and said: "You must come in to me, for I have hired you with my son's mandrakes." And he lay with her that night.

**28:26** God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son. Leah named him Issachar.

**28:27** Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son, and she named him Zebulun.

**28:28** Then Leah bore a daughter, and she named her Dinah.

**28:29** God remembered Rachel; God listened to her and opened her womb. She conceived and bore a son, and she named him Joseph.

**28:30** Rachel said: "God has taken away my reproach." And she said: "May the LORD add to me another son."

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering closely following LOGOS. The Jubilees chronological framework (jubilee/week/year) is preserved throughout. The birth sequence (vv.14-29) is the most systematic in any ancient source, assigning specific years to each birth. PNEUMA's vivid rendering of the mandrake exchange was consulted for nuance.*
